summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would let the Commonwealth impose charges for administering the new Road Vehicle Standards Bill, which would replace the Motor Vehicle Standards Act 1989 as the main law for regulating road vehicle imports and supply.

The charges would be set in regulations rather than in the bill itself, allowing the relevant minister to consult stakeholders and make timely adjustments while still being subject to parliamentary disallowance.
The bill specifically covers charges that amount to a duty of excise under section 55 of the Constitution, while companion bills cover customs and general charges.
changes: The bill would allow the Commonwealth to impose cost-recovery charges for activities connected with administering the Road Vehicle Standards Bill.
The bill would set charges through regulations rather than in primary legislation.
The bill would enable the government to develop National Road Vehicle Standards, maintain compliance and enforcement arrangements, and support consumers using the new system.
summary.affected: The explanatory memorandum says the charges would affect entities involved in importing or providing road vehicles in Australia, but does not name specific groups.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The Road Vehicle Standards Charges (Imposition-General) Bill 2018 was moved for a second reading, imposing charges to recover costs for regulating the first provision of road vehicles to the Australian market, with charges capped at no more than the Commonwealth's administrative costs.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The Road Vehicle Standards Charges (Imposition-Customs) Bill 2018 was moved for a second reading, imposing charges to recover costs for regulating first-provision road vehicles in Australia, with charges capped at the Commonwealth's administrative costs.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The Road Vehicle Standards Charges (Imposition-Excise) Bill 2018 was moved for a second reading, imposing charges for regulatory administration of the Road Vehicles Standards Bill 2018 and enabling cost recovery, with charges not set above the Commonwealth's likely costs.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The Road Vehicle Standards Bill 2018 and four companion bills were presented as a modern framework for regulating road vehicles, projected to save industry an estimated $20 million, establish the Register of Approved Vehicles (saving around $14 million a year), and introduce compulsory recall powers. The government announced amendments to allow used-vehicle imports for campervan/motorhome conversions, adjust power-to-weight thresholds for specialist vehicles, permit left-hand-drive heavy vehicles, and presented addenda to the explanatory memoranda following the Scrutiny of Bills committee's recommendations.
